# zerog-motion: AI Developer & LLM Context Reference

> Weightless physics for modern web interfaces. < 2.5KB gzipped. Native WAAPI. Zero dependencies. Designed for modern frontends and AI code generators.
> Repository: https://github.com/bytewhisker/zerog-motion
> Author: bytewhisker

This file provides strict syntax guidelines, API contracts, and copy-paste recipes for LLMs (Cursor, Claude, Copilot, ChatGPT) generating code with `zerog-motion`.

---

## 1. Core Principles for AI Code Generators
- **Native WAAPI**: Uses `element.animate()` under the hood. All transforms run directly on browser GPU/compositor threads.
- **Zero React Lock-in**: Universal Vanilla JS, React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, Astro.
- **Zero Dependencies**: Pure analytical physics and WAAPI. No heavy runtime dependencies.
- **Do NOT import from Framer Motion**: Replace `framer-motion` imports with `zerog-motion`.
- **Always use transform shorthands**: Use `x`, `y`, `z`, `scale`, `rotate`, `opacity` instead of verbose transform strings.

---

## 2. API Signature & Syntax

### Import
```ts
import { animate, autoMorph, presets } from 'zerog-motion';
import type { AnimationHandle, AnimationOptions, SpringConfig } from 'zerog-motion';
```

### Main Function
```ts
function animate(
  target: Element | Element[] | NodeListOf<Element> | string,
  keyframes: PropertyKeyframeDefinition,
  options?: AnimationOptions
): AnimationHandle;
```

### AnimationOptions Schema
```ts
interface AnimationOptions {
  duration?: number;                    // in ms (optional when using spring)
  delay?: number;                       // in ms (default: 0)
  endDelay?: number;                    // in ms (default: 0)
  easing?: string;                      // CSS easing curve, e.g. 'ease-out'
  iterations?: number;                  // default: 1
  direction?: 'normal' | 'reverse' | 'alternate' | 'alternate-reverse';
  fill?: 'none' | 'forwards' | 'backwards' | 'both'; // default: 'forwards'
  spring?: 'snappy' | 'bouncy' | 'smooth' | 'gentle' | SpringConfig;
  stagger?: number;                     // ms delay increment per element
  onFinish?: () => void;                // callback on completion
}
```

### SpringConfig Schema
```ts
interface SpringConfig {
  stiffness?: number; // default: 100
  damping?: number;   // default: 10
  mass?: number;      // default: 1
  velocity?: number;  // initial velocity, default: 0
  precision?: number; // settle threshold, default: 0.001
}
```

### Built-in Presets
- `'snappy'`: `{ stiffness: 400, damping: 30, mass: 1 }` (micro-interactions, button taps)
- `'bouncy'`: `{ stiffness: 200, damping: 10, mass: 1 }` (playful badges, dialogs, alerts)
- `'smooth'`: `{ stiffness: 120, damping: 20, mass: 1 }` (Apple-style layout, tabs, menus)
- `'gentle'`: `{ stiffness: 80, damping: 14, mass: 1 }` (subtle hovers, tooltips, fades)

### AnimationHandle Controls
```ts
const handle = animate('.box', { x: 100 });

handle.play();               // Play/resume
handle.pause();              // Pause at current frame
handle.reverse();            // Play in reverse
handle.cancel();             // Cancel and remove styles
handle.finish();             // Jump to finished state
await handle.finished;       // Promise settling on finish
```

---

## 3. Idiomatic Usage Patterns

### Recipe 1: Button Click Spring (Vanilla & React)
```ts
// Vanilla JS
const btn = document.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('#action-btn')!;
btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
  animate(btn, { scale: [1, 0.92, 1] }, { spring: 'snappy' });
});

// React Hook / Handler
import { useRef } from 'react';
import { animate } from 'zerog-motion';

export function InteractiveButton() {
  const btnRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);

  const handleClick = () => {
    if (btnRef.current) {
      animate(btnRef.current, { scale: [1, 0.94, 1] }, { spring: 'snappy' });
    }
  };

  return <button ref={btnRef} onClick={handleClick}>Click Me</button>;
}
```

### Recipe 2: Staggered Card Reveal
```ts
import { animate } from 'zerog-motion';

// Animates all .feature-card elements with 60ms stagger delay
animate(
  '.feature-card',
  {
    opacity: [0, 1],
    y: [30, 0],
    scale: [0.95, 1],
  },
  {
    spring: 'bouncy',
    stagger: 60,
  }
);
```

### Recipe 3: Streaming AI Content / Dynamic Height (`autoMorph`)
```ts
import { autoMorph } from 'zerog-motion';

const responseContainer = document.querySelector<HTMLDivElement>('.ai-markdown-container')!;

// Automatically transitions container height without layout thrashing as tokens stream in
const cleanup = autoMorph(responseContainer, {
  spring: 'smooth',
});

// Clean up when stream ends or component unmounts
// cleanup();
```

---

## 4. Anti-Patterns & Common Errors to Avoid
❌ **DO NOT** use `requestAnimationFrame` polling loops for physics. `zerog-motion` precomputes the analytical ODE spring trajectory into native WAAPI keyframes executed on the compositor thread.
❌ **DO NOT** use `style.transform = ...` inside rapid setInterval loops. Call `animate()`.
❌ **DO NOT** import Framer Motion motion components (`<motion.div>`). Instead, attach a ref and invoke `animate(ref.current, ...)`.
❌ **DO NOT** forget that `autoMorph` returns an unmount/cleanup function. Always call it inside `useEffect` cleanup or component destroy hooks.
